metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from China strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
Hey David, have you thought about what we should get Tom for his promotion? Maybe some flowers?

I was thinking... carnations could be nice. They’re simple but elegant.

What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... flowers are nice, but I wonder if we should give something more *meaningful*. Maybe a nice pen or a personalized gift? Something that symbolizes his achievement... What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message:
I mean, a pen is a good idea... but carnations have a certain charm. They still represent admiration and appreciation, which is important. 

But, uh, do you really think we need to go for something more meaningful? Sometimes simplicity speaks volumes...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it's all the same — flowers or a pen, as long as it's thoughtful, right? I think people figure it out. Simplicity can be charming, but we should also think about what really matters in this context. Anyway, about the gift... what if we add a nice card with a message? That could make it special, don’t you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: David
turns.message:
A card... yeah, that could add a personal touch. I can agree on that. 

But I still think carnations stand out in their own way. They are not just flowers; they hold significance too. 

By the way, do you think making our parents proud is really, uh, one of our main goals in life? I just... I don't know if I fully align with that belief.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: Well, for me, making my parents proud has always been a priority. It's a deep-rooted value in my culture... I feel like it's important to honor their sacrifices. That sense of pride, it really drives me. But I understand if you see it differently. I just... I can't help but feel that I've achieved something when my family is proud of me. What else do you think is important?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: David
turns.message:
I get that it's important to you, but for me, it's... it's different. I don't think pride from parents is a main goal. Achievements mean something on their own, without that pressure. 

I respect your view, but I just don't feel that same drive. 

Anyway, back to Tom... do you think carnations can still be a part of a thoughtful gift?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message:
I see your point, but I still believe that family pride can really amplify our achievements. It adds a layer of meaning. But if you feel differently, that’s okay... 

As for Tom, maybe we can use the carnations as part of the gift with a nice pen? That way, we combine both ideas — the charm of flowers and the symbolism of the pen. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: David
turns.message:
Combining them could work... I can see how that brings both elements together. 

I just hope the carnations aren't overshadowed by the pen. They should still hold their significance. 

But, uh, just to clarify, do you think family pride is truly essential? Because, for me, that’s... not really a driving force.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message:
I understand your perspective, but for me, family pride is *essential*. It motivates me to strive for success and honor my parents' hard work. Without that connection, it feels like something is missing. I respect your view, but I can't shake off the importance of that pride in my life... 

So, back to Tom, how about we plan to include a note with the carnations that expresses admiration? It can highlight their significance while still being part of the gift.
turns.label: Acceptance
